headline: US consumer one-year inflation expectations fall to 3.7% in November
summary: US one-year consumer inflation expectations fell from 4.7% in October to 3.7% in November, reaching their lowest level since February, according to the University of Michigan survey. Consumer sentiment rose to 51.5.
why: Consumer inflation expectations influence actual price pressures and wage demand, forming a key dataset monitored by the Federal Reserve.

impacts.name: US 10-year Treasury yield
impacts.why: Softening inflation expectations reduce market pressure on the Federal Reserve to raise policy rates aggressively.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: Lower inflation expectations eased trader concerns over prolonged monetary tightening by the Federal Reserve.
